content.title: About
content.content: Cherry pie is a baked dessert consisting of a flaky crust filled with fresh or canned cherries sweetened with sugar and flavored with vanilla or cinnamon. The crust is usually crisp, while the filling is juicy and slightly tart.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cherry pie is considered a classic American dessert, especially popular during the summer season.
Traditional recipes often feature a double crust – bottom and top, sometimes with a lattice design.
Cherries are rich in antioxidants, particularly anthocyanins, which give them their bright red color.
In the United States, cherry pie is frequently served with a scoop of vanilla ice cream – "à la mode".
The dish likely originated in Europe in the 19th century when cherries became widely available.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cherries contain anthocyanins that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Cherries provide vitamin C, supporting the immune system.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber in cherries promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many desserts, cherry pie can be made with modest amounts of butter.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Traditional pies contain a lot of sugar, which can be an issue for people with diabetes.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The crust usually contains wheat flour, making it unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Tart cherries may irritate the stomach of individuals with high acidity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Pie is fairly calorie‑dense due to crust and sugar; moderate consumption is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve cherry pie warm, often with a scoop of vanilla ice cream, whipped cream, or a light dusting of powdered sugar. Cut into portions and keep refrigerated for up to 3 days.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the pie in an airtight container in the refrigerator. It can also be frozen for up to 2 months; reheat in the oven at 180 °C before serving to restore a crisp crust.
